For the function $y=f(x)$ above, where does the function have a discontinuity due to a vertical asymptote?
question.worked_solution:
The function has discontinuities due to vertical asymptotes at $x=\pm 2.$ Note that

$$
{lim}_{x\to (-2)^{+}}f(x)=-\infty ,
$$

which is enough to conclude that there is a discontinuity due to a vertical asymptote at $x=-2.$ Similarly

$$
{lim}_{x\to {2}^{-}}f(x)=\infty ,
$$

which is enough to conclude that there is a discontinuity due to a vertical asymptote at $x=2.$

There is also a discontinuity at $x=0,$ but this is not a discontinuity due to a vertical asymptote.
